intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that orofaciodigital syndrome XVIII (OFD18) is caused by homozygous mutation in the IFT57 gene (606621) on chromosome 3q13.

checks.claim: Orofaciodigital syndrome XVIII (OFD18) is caused by homozygous mutation in the IFT57 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: we report on a unique consanguineous family with 3 affected siblings with an unclassified OFDS subtype with short stature and brachymesophalangia, harboring a homozygous IFT57 hypomorphic splice mutation
checks.explanation: The paper calls the disorder an unclassified OFDS; 'OFD18' is the OMIM label for it.

checks.claim: The IFT57 gene is located on chromosome 3q13.
checks.evidence_quote: an IFT57 synonymous variation (chr3:g.107910368C>T, c.777G>A, p.Lys259Lys, RefSeq accession number NM_018010.3)
checks.explanation: The paper places the gene on chromosome 3 but does not name the band; 3q13 is standard location nomenclature.

paragraphs.text: Orofaciodigital syndrome XVIII is a type of oral-facial-digital syndrome (OFDS) with short stature and brachymesophalangia. It overlaps with Ellis-van Creveld syndrome (EVCS). Thevenon et al. (2016) found that the disorder was caused by a homozygous hypomorphic mutation in IFT57 and called it the first description of a ciliary transport defect in OFDS.

checks.evidence_quote: we report on a unique consanguineous family with an unclassified type of OFDS with short stature and brachymesophalangia overlapping with EVCS

checks.claim: Orofaciodigital syndrome XVIII overlaps with Ellis-van Creveld syndrome (EVCS).
checks.evidence_quote: we report on a unique consanguineous family with an unclassified type of OFDS with short stature and brachymesophalangia overlapping with EVCS

checks.claim: Thevenon et al. (2016) found that orofaciodigital syndrome XVIII was caused by a homozygous hypomorphic mutation in IFT57.
checks.evidence_quote: and caused by a homozygous hypomorphic mutation of IFT57, affecting splicing and altering protein function.

checks.claim: Thevenon et al. (2016) described the IFT57 finding as the first description of a ciliary transport defect in OFDS.
checks.evidence_quote: highlights the first description of a ciliary transport defect in OFDS

paragraphs.text: Phadke et al. (1999) reported sibs from a consanguineous family who had a new variety of oral-facial-digital syndrome. In addition to oral, facial, and digital malformations, the sibs had acromelic short stature and genu valgum. The authors noted that these features overlap with Ellis-van Creveld syndrome. One sib also had urinary incontinence and growth hormone deficiency. The authors stated that neither feature had been reported before in any type of OFDS.

paragraphs.text: Thevenon et al. (2016) restudied the consanguineous Indian family first reported by Phadke et al. (1999). It included 3 affected sibs who had been followed for 15 years. One sib (II-3) died at 17 years of a complicated pulmonary infection. Subject II-1 was a male examined at 25 years. He had normal intelligence and short stature (155 cm, -3 SD). His facial and oral features were a square face with a short forehead, upslanting palpebral fissures, a high nasal bridge, a pyriform nose, a short philtrum, a medial cleft of the upper lip, supernumerary frenulae, and missing incisors. His limb features were pronounced brachydactyly, postaxial polydactyly of the upper limbs, and preaxial polydactyly of the feet due to duplication of the first metatarsal. X-rays showed severe mesophalangeal shortening, short femoral necks with varus femurs, and genu valgum. There was no thoracic deformity and there were no vertebral anomalies. Heart, renal, and abdominal ultrasounds were normal.

paragraphs.text: Subject II-2 in the family reported by Thevenon et al. (2016) was a female examined at 22 years. She had normal intelligence and short stature (122 cm, -5 SD). Her facial and oral features were a square face, a narrow forehead, enophthalmos, upslanting palpebral fissures, a broad nasal bridge, bilateral hypopigmented pseudoclefts, a medial labial cleft, missing incisors, and supernumerary frenulae. She had marked brachydactyly and postaxial polydactyly of all 4 limbs. X-rays showed: - mesophalangeal shortening, fused proximal phalanges, and bifid distal phalanges - duplication of the first metatarsal with absent middle phalanges (preaxial polydactyly) - vertebral bodies with medial notches, without platyspondyly - bilateral cervical ribs - gracile long bones and short femoral necks She had no thoracic deformity. Brain MRI and abdominal and heart ultrasounds were normal.

paragraphs.text: Thevenon et al. (2016) studied 3 sibs from a consanguineous Indian family with an unclassified OFDS with short stature and brachymesophalangia, originally reported by Phadke et al. (1999). Using homozygosity mapping and exome sequencing, they identified a homozygous synonymous variant in the IFT57 gene: a c.777G-A transition (p.Lys259Lys; NM_018010.3) affecting the last base of exon 6. Sanger sequencing confirmed that all 3 affected sibs were homozygous. The variant was not found in the ExAC database or in 50 healthy northern Indian controls. In patient fibroblasts, the variant caused a complex splicing pattern. Normal transcript was present along with 3 aberrant transcripts: - in-frame skipping of exon 6 - in-frame skipping of exons 5 and 6 - out-of-frame skipping of exons 4 through 6 The aberrant transcripts were detected only after inhibition of nonsense-mediated decay. IFT57 mRNA levels were reduced. These findings were consistent with a hypomorphic allele.

paragraphs.text: Thevenon et al. (2016) found that fibroblasts from the patients had a normal number and length of primary cilia but reduced anterograde ciliary transport. IFT57 staining at the ciliary tip was significantly decreased (90% vs 35%), and staining at the basal body was increased. Stimulation with SAG produced poor induction of GLI1 mRNA in patient fibroblasts. siRNA knockdown of IFT57 in control fibroblasts abolished GLI1 induction. These results indicated defective sonic hedgehog signaling, and the authors suggested that this defect underlies many of the phenotypes.

paragraphs.text: Thevenon et al. (2016) studied 3 affected sibs from a consanguineous Indian family with orofaciodigital syndrome XVIII (OFD18), first reported by Phadke et al. (1999). They identified a homozygous c.777G-A transition in the IFT57 gene (NM_018010.3). The transition affects the last base of exon 6 and does not change the amino acid (lys259-to-lys; K259K). The variant was found by homozygosity mapping and exome sequencing, and Sanger sequencing confirmed it. It was not found in the ExAC database or in 50 healthy northern Indian controls. In patient fibroblasts, normal transcript was present along with 3 aberrant transcripts: - in-frame skipping of exon 6 - in-frame skipping of exons 5 and 6 - out-of-frame skipping of exons 4 through 6 The aberrant transcripts were detected only after inhibition of nonsense-mediated decay. IFT57 mRNA levels were reduced, consistent with a hypomorphic allele. Patient fibroblasts also showed reduced anterograde ciliary transport and poor induction of GLI1 after SAG stimulation.
